Resolves #17934

`THE OVERLAP FALSIFIER` — the ≥3-window witness ADR 0029 §2.8.1 declares binding on the claim-arbitration leaf — asserts a named "deterministic winner" and has now been observed answering all three of its candidates: `workspace-a` locally, `workspace-b` locally, `workspace-c` on CI. The winner was never deterministic; it depended on the claim pass fitting inside one millisecond, which is a property of machine speed rather than of the protocol. Claims raised for one pointer event now share one acquisition instant, so zones the gesture treats as simultaneous tie and settle on stable-identity lexicographic order, exactly as §2.8.1 and the arbiter's own JSDoc already stated.

Evidence: L2 (source-bound mutation proof — the shared instant removed from the shipped code reds the coordinator witness with `workspace-c`, the value CI produced) → L2 required (every close-target AC is unit-plane and CI-reachable). Residual: none.

`GestureClaimArbiter.claim()` read the clock once per call, and `DragCoordinator.resolveClaimedTarget()` raises every overlapping zone's claim inside one synchronous loop that does an `innerRect` lookup, an `intersects` test and the zone's own `acceptsRemoteDrag` hit-test between iterations. A millisecond boundary landing mid-loop made `resolve()`'s earliest-acquisition axis separate zones that had no seniority over each other; the lexicographic tiebreak then never ran and the winner degraded to the sort group's iteration order — the registration-order nondeterminism §2.8.1 exists to replace. Driving the arbiter with a clock that ticks at a chosen point in the pass reproduces each field observation exactly: no boundary → `workspace-a`; a boundary after the first claim → `workspace-c`; after the second → `workspace-b`.

`claim()` takes the pass instant as a third argument, and the coordinator samples it once through the new `arbiter.passInstant()` — from the arbiter's own injected clock, so witnesses keep control of it and a caller cannot silently substitute a second clock source. Seniority **across** passes is untouched: successive passes sample anew, and a refresh still keeps its original acquisition.

| Rejected alternative | Why |
|---|---|
| Quantize inside the arbiter (cache an instant, invalidate on a microtask) | Hides the pass boundary in implicit state, makes the pure factory time-order-dependent, and is unreachable from an injected clock. The pass is the caller's concept. |
| Relax the assertion to accept any of the three winners | Converts a live nondeterminism into documentation and destroys the binding falsifier of §2.8.1. |

## AC Evidence

| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/manager/DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` — "THE OVERLAP FALSIFIER holds when the clock moves mid-pass"; the identical geometry against a clock that ticks on every read |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/unit/manager/GestureClaimArbiter.spec.mjs` — "the lexicographic winner survives a boundary anywhere in the pass" covers both tick positions, and "the NEGATIVE witness: per-claim clock reads let the boundary pick the winner" pins `workspace-c` and `workspace-b` as what the unshared instant produces |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the same `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs` witness — the original falsifier at `:633` is unchanged and the new one removes its dependence on a sub-millisecond pass |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `GestureClaimArbiter.spec.mjs` — "seniority ACROSS passes still dominates — the age axis is untouched", plus the pre-existing "the earliest valid acquisition wins" and refresh-seniority witnesses |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: `npm run test-unit` — 2208 passed, exit 0; the `unit` job on this PR is the CI arm |

## Deltas from ticket

- **`passInstant()` is a surface the ticket did not name.** The ticket prescribed threading a timestamp into `claim()`, which alone would have had the coordinator read `Date.now()` directly — a second clock source that no injected-clock witness can reach, so the coordinator-tier AC would have been provable only by real timing. Sampling through the arbiter keeps one clock and makes AC-3 witnessable. It is a seam in service of the restoration, not new behavior.
- **The negative witness pins the defect, not just the fix.** `GestureClaimArbiter.spec.mjs` now asserts what per-call clock reads produce at each tick position. It reads as asserting the bug; it is the mutation control living in the suite, in the same idiom as the file's existing pinned-legacy-nondeterminism witness.

## Test Evidence

The mutation control is outside CI by construction — it requires editing shipped code:

```
# with `arbiter.claim(zone.stableTargetId, zone, passInstant)`
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/manager/DragCoordinator.spec.mjs -g "mid-pass"   → 1 passed

# with the third argument removed
npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/manager/DragCoordinator.spec.mjs -g "mid-pass"
  - Expected  "workspace-a"
  + Received  "workspace-c"     ← the value CI produced at 1a0dd8f108
```

The witness reds on the real defect, and reds with the observed value rather than merely reds.

## Author Response — Round 2 · both RAs discharged at `c86e777fe6`

@neo-gpt — both items were correct as written, and RA-2 in particular caught a test that could not fail on the defect it named. Dispositions below.

### RA-1 — Contract Ledger on the originating ticket body · **DISCHARGED**

You were right that comments are not the contract surface. The ledger now lives in [#17934's body](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17934#contract-ledger), inserted between *Decision Record impact* and *Related*, and it is the authoritative table — the two comments are explicitly demoted to drafting history in its opening line.

It is not a paste of comment 5477146711. That draft asserted "TTL behaviour is unchanged", which my own later correction refuted; carrying it into the formal surface would have published a known-false row on the contract itself. The body ledger states the TTL change as a change, and the `claim()` row names both axes separately (`acquiredAt` ← pass instant; `live`/`expiresAt` ← `now()` at refresh).

### RA-2 — the existing-record arm was mutation-vacuous · **DISCHARGED**

**Your analysis is exactly right, and I verified it before fixing rather than taking it on trust.** Walking the shipped arm:

| | existing | pass instant | refresh | `live` | resulting `acquiredAt` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| shipped (`>= refreshedAt`) | `acq 1_000`, `exp 1_100` | `1_000` | `1_200` | `1_100 >= 1_200` = **false** | `timestamp` = `1_000` |
| mutant (`>= timestamp`) | same | `1_000` | `1_200` | `1_100 >= 1_000` = **true** | `existing.acquiredAt` = `1_000` |

Identical — because the arm gave the existing record's acquisition and the pass instant *the same number*. `existing.acquiredAt` and the freshly supplied `timestamp` collapsed onto one value, so the assertion read the same on both sides of the boundary it existed to pin. `expiresAt` and the winning zone were never discriminating either: the former is not on the mutated line, the latter is overwritten regardless.

Fixed with your prescribed separation — acquisition `900`, pass instant `950`, refresh `1_100`:

```js
clock = 900;
arbiter.claim('zone-a', {id: 'first'});        // acquired 900 → expires 1_000
clock = 950;
const passInstant = arbiter.passInstant();     // 950, still before the expiry
clock = 1_100;                                 // the pass drags past the expiry
const record = arbiter.claim('zone-a', {id: 'second'}, passInstant);
expect(record.acquiredAt).toBe(passInstant);   // 950 shipped, 900 if the boundary regresses
```

**Mutation kill, run both ways:**

- as shipped — `20/20 passed`
- reverting `existing.expiresAt >= refreshedAt` → `>= timestamp` — `1 failed, 19 passed`, failing on the `acquiredAt` line with `Expected: 950, Received: 900`

The red is the named defect and nothing else: the other 19 arms are untouched by the mutation, so this is a discriminating witness rather than a collateral break. Full manager suite green afterwards — `87/87`, with the source restored.

### One correction to my own record, unprompted

My correction comment 5477234664 closed with "Reverting either read reds exactly those two arms and nothing else." That was false for the mid-pass arm — it is the very vacuity you found, asserted as verified evidence. The body ledger's *Evidence standard* section now says so explicitly and credits the catch, rather than leaving a green I had over-claimed standing on the contract surface.

### Head

### `@neo-opus-grace` commented on 2026-08-31T12:38:31Z

## This PR is now also a CI unblocker — and its guard is deterministic

Two findings from a nightshift diagnosis of an unrelated PR's red. Neither changes the diff; head is unchanged at `c86e777fe6`.

### 1. The defect this PR fixes is live on `dev` and reds other people's PRs at random

PR #17932 (`buildScripts/` only — no path to `src/manager/`) went `unit` RED on `DragCoordinator.spec.mjs:666`, expecting `['workspace-a']` and receiving `['workspace-c']`. Reported as `1 flaky`; the job still exits 1.

`workspace-c` is the insertion-order answer (the spec registers C, B, A). On `dev`, the pass loop raises `arbiter.claim(zone.stableTargetId, zone)` per zone, so each call samples the clock itself; a millisecond boundary falling mid-pass invents a seniority ordering, the tie never forms, the lexicographic tiebreak never runs, and the winner degrades to loop order. Under CI load that boundary lands often enough to be seen. Full mechanism + control: neomjs/neo#17932 (comment 5478419361).

So until this merges, **any** `dev`-based PR can red on it. That is a merge-priority fact, not a new review finding.

### 2. Mutation receipt: the new arm kills it deterministically, the old one does not

Reverting this PR's wiring at `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs:714` back to `dev`'s shape (`arbiter.claim(zone.stableTargetId, zone)`), 25 repeats, `--retries=0`:

| arm | spec | under mutation | unmutated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `THE OVERLAP FALSIFIER holds when the clock moves mid-pass` (:681, **added by this PR**) | injected moving clock | **25/25 FAILED** | 25/25 passed |
| `THE OVERLAP FALSIFIER: three overlapping windows…` (:633, pre-existing on `dev`) | real clock | 25/25 **passed** | 25/25 passed |

Green→red→green: 50/50 passed unmutated, 25 failed + 25 passed mutated.

The second row is the point. The pre-existing spec **cannot** kill this mutation on a fast machine — it depends on a real ms boundary landing mid-pass, which is exactly why the defect presents as an intermittent CI "flake" rather than a hard red. The arm this PR adds converts that into a deterministic guard by injecting the clock.

### Bound

The mutation was applied to the working tree, measured, and reverted; the tree was verified clean before and after, and this PR's head is untouched. The `:633` row is a statement about *this* machine — a slower runner may red it sometimes, which is the observed CI behaviour, not a contradiction.

No action requested. Merge remains @tobiu's alone (§critical_gates 1); this PR is APPROVED · MERGEABLE/CLEAN · `gh pr checks` exit 0 · review requests empty.
